fields.explanation: The point F = 9/4, B = 43043/100000 satisfies the printed interval and affine relation. Mathlib exact real decimal arithmetic proves that the displayed surrogate is strictly above the printed alleged upper bound, with the two values stated in the witness. This isolates that one numerical inequality in an auxiliary case calculation of the appendix; it is not a counterexample to the paper's theorem or to the surrounding lemma. The two printed coefficients 102.618907 and −473.377198 also appear in the neighbouring case display of the same appendix; no cause is asserted.

fields.witness: Take F = 9/4 = 2.25 and B = 43043/100000 = 0.43043. Then 2.226 < F ≤ 2.26 and B = −24.116548·F + 54.692663 exactly. At this point the displayed surrogate 0.246345·B² + (18.810319·F − 42.033351)·B + 202.972148·F² − 924.926294·F + 1052.803636 equals −1127237140734619/2000000000000000 (≈ −0.5636), whereas the asserted upper bound 102.618907·F² − 473.377198·F − 509.223573 equals −16877024829/16000000 (≈ −1054.81). Since −0.5636 > −1054.81, surrogate > asserted bound, so the displayed '≤' fails at an admissible point. The selected Lean theorem certifies exactly these four facts with exact decimal arithmetic: 2.226 < F, F ≤ 2.26, the affine relation for B, and surrogate > assertedBound.
